status_summary: Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) removed the end dates of the 2017 suspensions of miscellaneous itemized deductions and of the moving expense exclusion, and struck the bicycle commuting exclusion, for tax years beginning after 2025, while carving out educator expenses from the itemized-deduction suspension and adding an intelligence community exception to the moving rule beside the military one. It also ended the section 179D energy-efficient commercial building deduction for property whose construction begins after 2026-06-30. On the state and local tax deduction it went the other way in the near term, raising the cap from 10,000 to 40,000 dollars for 2025 and 40,400 dollars for 2026, rising 1 percent a year through 2029 with a 30 percent phase-down above modified adjusted gross income of 500,000 dollars for 2025 and 505,000 dollars for 2026 that cannot lower the cap below 10,000 dollars, and then returning to a 10,000 dollar cap that no longer expires. The student loan interest deduction remains in the Code.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 section 70110 removed the end date of the suspension of miscellaneous itemized deductions (26 U.S.C. 67), with an educator-expense exception, for tax years beginning after 2025.

Public Law 119-21 sections 70112 and 70113 struck the bicycle commuting exclusion from 26 U.S.C. 132 and removed the end date of the moving expense exclusion suspension, keeping the military exception and adding one for intelligence community employees, for tax years beginning after 2025.

Public Law 119-21 section 70120 raised the state and local tax deduction cap in 26 U.S.C. 164(b) to 40,000 dollars for 2025 and 40,400 dollars for 2026, rising 1 percent a year through 2029, with a 30 percent phase-down above modified adjusted gross income of 500,000 dollars for 2025 and 505,000 dollars for 2026 that cannot lower the cap below 10,000 dollars, and a 10,000 dollar cap with no end date from 2030.
Public Law 119-21 section 70507 added a termination to 26 U.S.C. 179D for property whose construction begins after 2026-06-30.

title: Repeal suspended deductions, the SALT deduction and the 179D building deduction
uncertainties: Route read: Cornell Legal Information Institute copies of 26 U.S.C. 164, 179D, 67 and 132 with their Public Law 119-21 amendment notes (reread in this review), plus the official enrolled text on govinfo.gov, of which only the opening part (the table of contents and title I) could be loaded; that part confirms the section numbers and headings of sections 70110, 70112, 70113, 70120 and 70507 but not their operative text, so the substance rests on the Cornell copy, which is not the official Code. Section 221 and the H.R. 1 bill status record were read by the researcher. The notes do not use the word permanent; permanence is inferred from the removed end dates. Under the 2017 law the 10,000 dollar cap would have expired after 2025, so the new law also keeps a cap in place for good, which can be read as partly consistent with limiting the deduction; the record treats the higher cap through 2029 as the opposite of full repeal. Other education items and the full list of 2017 suspensions (for example the personal exemption) were not reviewed. The state and local tax item also appears in c22-02, which tracks it as moving opposite to the text. Mixed-package rule applied: two element groups enacted as asked (the suspensions and 179D) against one opposite (SALT) and one with no repeal and a small opposite carve-out (education).
